title: Focus Lab — personal OKR journal (Q2) — Noah Lee
content:
(Quick note: this is my personal lab for OKR planning + weekly logs — messy, iterative. Keep it lean.)

Quarter: Q2 2024
Role: Staff SWE, serving-runtime
Purpose: track personal contribution to team OKRs (latency/cost/quality), run small experiments, and keep a running retrospective so weekly work becomes measurable.

Objective (O): Reduce tail latency and per-token cost for the hosted text-generation surface in the most common production workloads.
Key Results (KRs):
  KR1: Reduce P99 generation latency (1k token context) by 15% for model-xyz-13b (baseline P99: 680ms).
  KR2: Cut per-token inference cost by 12% through batching/quantization recommendations adopted by Dedicated.
  KR3: Ship two small rollout features for graceful fallback (region + model variant routing) and measure customer impact (<=1% error budget).
  KR4: Run and document 3 evaluation suites comparing output quality pre/post quantization (pass threshold: no more than 3% regression on eval prompts).

Baselines & metrics (current, 2024-03-11):
  - model-xyz-13b P50: 210ms, P90: 420ms, P99: 680ms
  - avg tokens/sec per GPU: 125
  - unit token cost (hosted): $0.00095/token (aggregate)
  - customer-facing errors attributed to fallback: 0.6% last 30d

Planned experiments (priority order):
  1) Mini-quant pipeline: fast 4-bit quant for encoder/decoder slices + validate on 1000 eval prompts. (hypothesis: ~8-10% cost reduction, small quality regressions manageable)
  2) Dynamic batching policy tweak: prioritize small interactive sessions at p50, but increase batching window to capture throughput spikes during bulk jobs. (hypothesis: better avg throughput with controlled SLOs)
  3) KV-prefix caching for chat sessions with repeat system prompts — measure cache hit improvement and token savings.

Weekly log (sparse + honest)
  2024-03-12 (kickoff): drafted KRs, captured baselines, pinged Aisha for eval harness access. Notes: need standardized prompt set; ask research for curated 200 prompts.
  2024-03-18: ran initial micro-quant on local node — surfaced tensor layout mismatch; opened RINF-1234 (linked above).
  2024-03-22: meeting with Infra (Ben) — confirmed we can spin a dedicated test pool with same kernel selection as staging. Ben will provision by 03/26.
  2024-03-28: first eval results (100 prompts): 7.4% cost reduction estimate, quality delta (BLEU-like proxy) ~1.8% regression on edge cases. Need wider eval.
  2024-03-31: retro note: need better gating for regressions — proposed a 3-tier fail/pass/warn system tied to rollout policy.
  2024-04-02: consolidated next steps list and prioritized tickets for sprint.

Next steps (short):
  - [ ] Acquire full 1k prompt set from research (Aisha) and schedule evaluation run (Ben).
  - [ ] Harden quant conversion scripts (edge case: attention weights) — allocate 2 days.
  - [ ] Create canary rollout plan for model-variant fallback (doc skeleton in Confluence).
  - [ ] Add telemetry slice for prefix-cache hit rate and token cost per session.

Blockers / unknowns:
  - Convergence of eval metric to customer-perceived quality — need product to sign off on tolerance.
  - GPU kernel mismatch on one of our testing nodes (intermittent) — infra debug in progress.
  - Coordination with Dedicated team on pricing experiments requires a short sync.

Retrospective rubric (how I’ll grade progress at end of quarter):
  - Metric movement: Did P99 and cost change in the expected direction? (hard number)
  - Adoption: Did team/Dedicated adopt any of my recommendations? (yes/no + percent)
  - Quality: Did evals stay within the 3% regression budget?
  - Learning: Were there 3 concrete lessons or new automations I shipped?

Personal timeboxing notes (to avoid context switching):
  - Monday: setup / experimentation day (blocked for deep work)
  - Wednesday: sync + review day (meetings with infra, research)
  - Friday: write-up & retrospective clip (capture notes while fresh)

Quick wins I can ship in 1-week sprints:
  - small telemetry view for prefix cache hit rates (dashboard stub)
  - script to convert model weights with safer fallback path (adds ~1 hour of CI tests)
  - checklist for canary rollout that ties into console alerts

Notes to self: write concise playbook after each experiment. If a result looks good but the eval set is small, mark it as "pilot" not "done". Keep communication simple: numbers + ask (e.g., "I need you to review these 3 prompts and confirm tolerances").

Links / quick refs: RINF-1234 (quant pipeline), RINF-1288 (canary routing design), confluence page for perf-evals (linked above).

End of page. Will reuse this doc for weekly check-ins and then convert to a cleaned one-pager when KRs are stable.
